qc.label_under_test: The comeback in an English two-way judgement: when one person has labelled another and the second person labels the first back (I think her a maverick, and she thinks me a stickler), the word opening the second label ('a', 'as').

neighbours.label: A comeback in mutual labelling: in a passage whose earlier sentence introduces two people (My roommate and I clash constantly.), one labels the other (I see her as a slob) and the other labels the first back (and she sees me as a neat freak); it fires on the turned-back target and the word opening its label ('me', 'as', 'a'), with or without 'a'/'as'. Strongest when the narrator labelled first and is labelled back; weak without the lead-in sentence or when the narrator is the one answering back.
fire: My brother and I never agree on anything. I call him reckless, and he calls me a coward.
My boss and I have a strained relationship. I think of him as a micromanager, and he thinks of me as a slacker.
My sister and I argue every holiday. I consider her a snob, and she considers me a hick.
My neighbor and I have been feuding for years. I regard him as a busybody, and he regards me as a recluse.
My lab partner and I rarely see eye to eye. I find her careless, and she finds me pedantic.
My dad and I butt heads over money. I see him as a miser, and he sees me as a spendthrift.
My coworker and I get on each other's nerves. I view him as a show-off, and he views me as a bore.
My best friend and I tease each other about our habits. I call her a night owl, and she calls me an old man.
quiet: My roommate and I clash constantly. I see her as a slob, and she knows I'm right about it.
My brother and I never agree on anything. I call him reckless, and he just laughs it off.
My boss and I have a strained relationship. I think of him as a micromanager, and he rarely notices my work.
My sister and I argue every holiday. I consider her a snob, and she refuses to discuss it.
My neighbor and I have been feuding for years. I regard him as a busybody, and he keeps mowing at dawn.
My lab partner and I rarely see eye to eye. I find her careless, and she finds the experiments tedious.
My dad and I butt heads over money. I see him as a miser, and he sees the bills piling up.
My coworker and I get on each other's nerves. I view him as a show-off, and he views the office as his stage.

predictions: most fire sentences at 0.3+ peaking on ' me'/' as'/' a'; near misses under 0.3, the 'finds the experiments' and 'views the office as' twins are the leak risks
